title: Definition of content model doesn't play well with its definition on some elements
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The [content model](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#concept-element-content-model) of an element is defined as "A normative description of what content must be included as children and descendants of the element."

A lot of the time, this is fine.
Many elements, however, just list their content model as [Flow Content](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#flow-content-2), [Phrasing Content](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#phrasing-content-2) or similar.
When you click on those, you just get a list of elements.

So the question came up: Do I need at least one of those? Zero or more? ~~All of them?~~

For what it's worth, some elements have a content model of [Text](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#text-content), which does explicitly say that, as a content model, it may be nothing.

So probably either Flow Content and such should include that, as a content model, they mean zero or more of the listed elements, or the content model for things like the [body](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-body-element) element should be changed to explicitly allow any or none of those elements.
